title: Pre-Analysis (Closed) — Crew Mask Hose Sleeve, Proposed Inspection Interval Relief
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of an operator request to extend the crew mask hose inspection interval on aircraft carrying the sleeved hose, rejected because the sleeve hides the cover damage the inspection exists to find.

sections.objective: Establish whether the five year hose condition inspection could be extended on aircraft embodying the sleeved hose and guide bracket, as requested by two operators at the technical review.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and the request was rejected. The controlling argument came from the modification itself: the woven sleeve protects the cover but also conceals it, so an inspection on a sleeved hose is less informative than on an unsleeved one, not more. The removal task records abrasion depth against limits that assume a visible cover, and no equivalent criterion exists for a sleeved hose. The crew limitation entry requires the mask to be withdrawn and donned with one hand at every preflight check, which is a daily functional check and was found to be the real protection against a trapped hose, but it says nothing about cover condition. Extending the interval would have removed the only condition check in the programme.
sections.next_steps: Request rejected. The operators were offered a sleeve inspection criterion instead, which was passed to the maintenance programme owner as a separate action.

similarity_seeds: a protective cover that also hides the damage the inspection looks for

tasks.title: Review the abrasion limits against a sleeved hose
Check what the crew preflight check actually detects

expected_findings.rationale: The removal task records abrasion depth against limits written for a visible cover. On a sleeved hose that measurement cannot be made without removing the sleeve, and no criterion exists for judging the sleeve itself.
expected_findings.resolution: Reject the interval relief until a sleeve inspection criterion exists.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin is linked to an airworthiness directive and its compliance rests on the inspection remaining in the maintenance programme at its published interval.
expected_findings.resolution: No change to the interval without an authority position on the directive.

evidence.similarity_note: The crew limitation describes a daily physical withdrawal of the mask, in crew language, and never mentions hose cover condition.

expected_findings.rationale: The preflight check is a daily functional check that would catch a trapped hose but tells nobody anything about cover wear, so it cannot substitute for the periodic inspection.
expected_findings.resolution: No change to the crew entry; recorded to show the substitution was considered.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure shows the two hose standards correctly and needs no change; recorded because the review checked it.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned on the interval and condition-check language, which is nearly identical, but it is a lavatory servicing task with no oxygen content and no shared identifier.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. Interval relief rejected; a sleeve inspection criterion was raised as a separate action.
